subject: OliveStack: repeated evaluation credit requests — risk review and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Flag: OliveStack repeated eval credit requests (June spike)

Mina / Soojin,

Sales Ops flagged OliveStack for an abnormal uptick in evaluation credit requests during June. Quick summary from my side:
- Multiple distinct "trial" requests from apparent siblings of the same org (three accounts referencing the same billing contact).
- Requests came in over 10 days and included repeated asks for top-up credits after initial grants.
- HubSpot shows the lead as active; a demo ran 6/8 but we also have fresh trial extensions granted 6/12, 6/20, 6/28.

I attached the usage export I pulled from the trial granting dashboard (olivestack_usage_report_2027-06.csv) — can you both take a look and advise if we should pause further promotional credits? If this looks like coordinated evaluation sharing, we should consider a temporary hold and a deeper audit.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) Quick log review (IP overlap, API keys reused, KV/cache footprints).
2) If suspicious, pause additional credit grants and escalate to Fraud Ops.
3) Notify the account contact with a polite hold message and ask for organizational verification.

Appreciate a quick read — I have a renewal call with them next week and don't want to give more credits without a thumbs up.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flag: OliveStack repeated eval credit requests (June spike)

Thanks Ben — forwarding to Soojin for the log pull and initial verdict.

Soojin: could you pull the following and drop an excerpt in this thread?
- API key usage map for all accounts in the OliveStack org for 6/1–6/30.
- IP address histogram and reverse DNS for those calls.
- KV cache access patterns and any evidence of shared prefix caches.

If you find clear reuse or scripted behavior, recommend we:
A) Pause auto-approvals for further trial/top-up requests for OliveStack.
B) Flag the relevant HubSpot records (DL-2027-OLV-09) with a fraud risk tag and next-contact instructions.

I will hold on external comms until we have a short summary to share.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flag: OliveStack repeated eval credit requests (June spike)

Attaching the requested excerpts: kv_cache_access_log_excerpt.txt and a cleaned usage CSV (see attachments). TL;DR of findings:

Summary findings (6/1–6/30):
- Four distinct Redwood accounts (ids redacted) requested eval/top-up credits; all list the same billing contact email (billing@olivestack.ai).
- API usage patterns show four unique API keys but identical hourly token-generation cadence between keys — consistent with a shared orchestration script.
- IP overlap: ~85% of traffic came from two CIDR ranges (54.213.0.0/16 and 3.90.0.0/16). Reverse DNS suggests AWS EC2 hosts registered to the same company block.
- KV cache: keys with identical prefixes observed across the accounts; timestamps show near-simultaneous cache priming events.

Assessment: high likelihood of coordinated evaluation sharing (accounts running distributed evaluation across multiple instances). Not 100% conclusive of fraud in the legal sense, but it violates our promo intent and increases unit cost with little evidence of separate product teams.

Recommendation:
1) Pause auto-approval of additional eval credits for OliveStack immediately.
2) Mark HubSpot deal DL-2027-OLV-09 as "promo_under_review" and notify sales to route any further credit requests through Sales Ops.
3) Ask the account for org-level verification (a simple org chart or confirmation of distinct product teams) before approving more grants.

I've uploaded the full log excerpt to the fraud review doc (link in related_links). Happy to run a more exhaustive check if Legal wants to weigh in.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Risk Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: sales_ops@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flag: OliveStack repeated eval credit requests (June spike)

Thanks Soojin — that's exactly the level of detail I needed. I support the pause.

Proposed external message (short):
- Let OliveStack know we've temporarily paused further promotional credits while we confirm account structure and usage.
- Offer a short, paid pilot or schedule a joint runbook to validate the use cases if they need more capacity for evaluation.

Mina — ready to send once you sign off on tone. I'd prefer we avoid "fraud" language; focus on "verification" and "fair use of promotional credits."

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Temporary hold on additional evaluation credits — OliveStack

Hi Jared,

Thanks for your continued engagement and for the demo last week — we appreciate OliveStack's interest in Redwood's batch inference features. I wanted to let you know weve placed a temporary hold on further automated evaluation credit grants for your account while we confirm a few details about how the trial is being used across your organization. This is a short, precautionary measure to make sure promo credits are applied in line with our evaluation program.

What were asking for (quick):
- A short confirmation of how many distinct product teams are evaluating Redwood and a single point of contact for each team (name + role + email).
- If convenient, an org chart or a short note from your CTO indicating the teams/testing groups that require access.

What we can offer immediately:
- If you need additional capacity to complete your evaluation, we can provide a 2-week paid pilot at a reduced rate while verification is in progress, or schedule a technical run with Ben and our Solutions Engineering team to validate workload patterns.

Please send the requested note or org chart and well process any approved top-up within 48 hours. If you prefer to discuss, we can hop on a 20-minute call — Ben is copied and can coordinate.

Thanks for understanding. We want to ensure OliveStack gets a productive evaluation and that credits are used in ways that reflect separate product evaluations where applicable.

Best,
